messages:
Marissa Cole: want to lock v1 scope for retention controls + reporting pack. Getting mixed answers from Eng/SE.

Specifically:
1) which datasets are in v1 (customer-configurable)
2) default retention by tier (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
3) what exactly ships in “compliance reporting pack v1”

Can folks confirm so we can update PM-482 + the Console copy?

Naomi Feldman: yep, +1. also need to align w/ guardrails (min/max) + legal hold semantics, so we don’t promise impossible configs.

Logan Wright: from telemetry side: we can do TTL / scheduled deletes for *some* analytics tables in v1. not for every raw log stream.

Ethan Park: control plane can support “policy types” even if some are no-op initially, but PM should be explicit what’s enforceable in v1 vs “informational”.

Marissa Cole: cool. let’s do a concrete list. Proposed v1 configurable datasets:
- Audit logs (security audit events)
- Admin activity (Console + API config changes)
- Inference request metadata (timestamps, model, token counts, status) **NOT** prompts/responses
- Telemetry/analytics eligible tables (aggregated usage + latency)
- Operational logs: only where we store them in Redwood-managed DBs (not vendor/SRE infra logs)

Anything missing / anything we should cut?

Chloe Martin: Console side: we can surface all of those as toggles/rows, but we need “(not available in your deployment)” states for Private vs Hosted. We’ll also need a very explicit line that raw prompts/responses retention is out of scope.

Naomi Feldman: agree w/ your list. I’d word “operational logs” carefully. Some customers interpret that as “everything in datadog/splunk/etc” which we can’t do. Maybe label it “Redwood operational datasets (selected)” and link to an inventory.

Olga Petrov: +1. from compliance: it’s OK if v1 says “some infra logs follow SRE standard retention” but we need to be able to *explain* it in the pack and show what is customer-configurable vs fixed.

Markus Klein: from SE/sales POV, the biggest confusion is “inference metadata” vs “payload”. We should give a one-liner definition + examples in the FAQ + pack.

Logan Wright: +1. Example: “we store request_id, model, region, token counts, latency, error code” for X days. We do NOT store prompt text by default (unless customer enables separate logging feature, which isn’t part of this project).

Marissa Cole: ok. on default retention by tier: what’s the current proposal? I’ve heard 30/90/365 floating around.

Naomi Feldman: what we discussed in product sync last week (tentative):
- Hosted (self-serve / default): 30 days
- Hosted (enterprise plan): 90 days default, configurable to 365
- Dedicated: 365 days default
- Private: customer-controlled, but we ship with safe default 90 days unless contract requires otherwise

Need to confirm with eng what max is realistic.

Ethan Park: guardrails proposal (consistent across):
- min retention: 7 days (to avoid “delete everything instantly” footgun + keep enough for incident triage)
- max retention: 7 years (we can store longer but it becomes “talk to us” / legal approval + cost)
- “never delete” should be disallowed unless legal hold OR explicitly enabled for Private with customer-owned storage

(reactions: :thumbsup: x4)

Chloe Martin: if we set max=7 years we need to be prepared to show “estimated storage impact” somewhere eventually. for v1 we can at least show a warning banner when >365.

Logan Wright: telemetry tables: max 13 months for some aggregated metrics is probably fine. but 7 years for *high-cardinality* stuff (per-request) isn’t.

Naomi Feldman: good call — we may need per-dataset max values (not one global max). Can we land on: “max varies by dataset, UI shows allowed range”? (that keeps us honest)

Ethan Park: yes. policy model supports per data_type min/max.

Marissa Cole: can we pin v1 defaults like this (subject to per-dataset caps):

Defaults (v1):
- Audit logs: Hosted 90d (Enterprise) / 30d (Self-serve); Dedicated 365d; Private 90d
- Admin activity: same as audit logs
- Inference request metadata: Hosted 30d; Dedicated 90d; Private 30d
- Telemetry/analytics (aggregated): Hosted 90d; Dedicated 13mo; Private 90d

Does that match eng feasibility + compliance posture?

Logan Wright: telemetry defaults look fine. I’d set Hosted aggregated to 30 or 60 days if we’re worried about cost, but 90 is OK if it’s aggregated not raw.

Naomi Feldman: I’m OK w/ those defaults. audit/admin at 90 for Hosted enterprise is important for reviews.

Olga Petrov: from audit perspective: 90d minimum for audit logs is a common ask, but we can still allow customers to lower it (down to 30?) if they want. The key is: UI should show “recommended” vs “allowed.”

Ethan Park: technically we can allow lower, but security team might want a floor. For audit logs I’d prefer min=30d even if global min=7d.

Naomi Feldman: +1, min by dataset:
- audit/admin min 30d
- request metadata min 7d
- aggregated telemetry min 30d

(reactions: :thumbsup: x3)

Marissa Cole: awesome. final item: “compliance reporting pack v1” contents. I want a crisp list we can hand to Sales + also use internally.

Olga Petrov: pack v1 should include:
1) Overview narrative (what retention controls are, which products: Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
2) Data retention matrix (dataset -> default retention -> configurable range -> enforcement method -> owner)
3) Audit logging coverage summary (what events are captured; where available)
4) Control-to-evidence mapping (SOC 2 / ISO-style) focused on retention + audit logging
5) Retention policy attestation page (effective policy screenshot/export + last enforcement run timestamp)
6) Evidence collection procedure (internal runbook: how to generate the pack + what artifacts to attach)

Markus Klein: can we include 1-2 “example artifacts” that customers always ask for?
- sample audit log export (csv/json)
- screenshot of Console retention settings showing effective policy

Olga Petrov: yes, as redacted examples.

Chloe Martin: for Console screenshots, let’s use staging tenant w/ a policy that demonstrates overrides + legal hold banner (if we have it by then).

Naomi Feldman: we should explicitly say what is *not* in pack v1:
- no SOC 2 report included (unless under NDA / separate process)
- no pentest report
- no claim that all infra logs are customer-configurable

Marissa Cole: +1. I’ll add “Not included” section to avoid over-interpretation.

Talia Benson: capturing decisions + action items:
- v1 configurable datasets: audit logs, admin activity, inference request metadata (no payload), selected telemetry/analytics tables, selected Redwood operational datasets (not vendor infra logs)
- defaults: align to Marissa’s table w/ per-dataset min/max (audit/admin min 30d; others min 7/30 as agreed). per-dataset max shown in UI.
- reporting pack v1: Olga’s 6 sections + sample artifacts + explicit exclusions.

Action items:
- Marissa: update PM-482 + Console copy draft w/ these defaults + dataset definitions
- Naomi/Olga: sanity check language for security reviews + exclusions
- Logan/Ethan: confirm per-dataset max ranges we can enforce in v1 and feed back to product by EOW

(reactions: :white_check_mark: x5)
